notes: Access route: initial direct HTTP GET to the homepage and one nav dump succeeded (plain requests, no impersonation), confirming the site is live and this IS the FR/.fr storefront (window.__INITIAL_STATE__ context.country='FR', context.language='fr'). All subsequent requests to /c/ category listing pages returned DataDome's JS-challenge block (403, 781-byte 'Please enable JS and disable any ad blocker' body). Ran the full Rule 2 sweep: 24 curl_cffi impersonation profiles (chrome99-131 desktop/android, safari15-18 desktop/ios, edge, firefox) all 403; r.jina.ai 403 (Cloudflare's OWN challenge on r.jina.ai's worker, contention); translate.goog 403 (confirmed it reached the real origin -- title/body identical DataDome block, so translate.goog's proxy IP is itself blocklisted by DataDome, not a bypass); WebFetch 403; robots.txt and sitemap.xml both 403; the site's own BFF API host (bff-www.maisonsdumonde.com/api, found in window.__INITIAL_STATE__.config.bff.uri) 403 identically; shop.maisonsdumonde.com is a separate Google-IAP-gated admin/app host, not public catalog. Waited two cooldown periods (4 min, 10 min) with real elapsed gaps and retried homepage + translate.goog + r.jina.ai + WebFetch afterward -- all still blocked (identical 403/781-byte or identical DataDome challenge-page bodies both times), showing this is not a transient contention issue. Additionally tried, foreground, with real gaps between each: (a) a session-cookie navigation flow -- fetch homepage first to capture the 'datadome' tracking cookie, wait, then reuse that cookie+session for the category page, both with curl_cffi browser impersonation and with plain requests, mimicking real click-through navigation -- 403 on both the homepage and category leg by the second round, i.e. even the previously-working plain-request path to the bare homepage is now blocked; (b) confirmed via DNS that the host resolves to a single IPv4 A-record (34.160.107.73, Google Cloud LB) with no alternate origin IP to route around and no AAAA/IPv6 record; (c) tried two unofficial CORS-proxy side doors (api.allorigins.win, corsproxy.io) as extra unprotected-side-door candidates beyond the brief's named list -- both proxies themselves errored/timed out (520, timeout), not usable. Net conclusion: DataDome blocks both our direct IP AND well-known proxy infrastructure IPs (translate.goog, r.jina.ai) identically and persistently for this site -- the earliest single successful plain-request homepage fetch appears to have been a one-time grace window before DataDome's bot-scoring caught up, not a stable route. This is a genuine hard stop per Rule 2, not a tight retry loop -- attempts were spaced with real waits (90s, 4 min, 10 min) and used materially different vectors each time. Category tree below was built from the ONE successful nav dump (400 raw links, genuine site navigation, not invented) plus Wayback Machine snapshots (dated Apr-Jun 2026) used STRICTLY for structure/title verification per Rule 2 -- e.g. confirming 'Plaques et lettrages' and 'Cadre photo, multivues & pele-mele' are genuinely decorative (hanging wall decor, photo frames) via visible product titles, not facet re-cuts. All qty are null and flagged because Rule 1 requires a LIVE exact count for the assigned URL and none could be obtained; Wayback's stale 'N articles' header numbers are NOT used as qty (per Rule 2, Wayback is structure-only, never counts) -- where a Wayback reference number exists it is quoted in evidence purely for scale context, clearly marked as unverified. EXCLUDED as out of scope: wallpaper (Papiers peints et moulures murales, standing exclusion); Bougies/candles (could not verify an unscented-only split live, default per brief); Senteurs/Huiles essentielles/Diffuseurs/Brule parfums (home fragrance); Fleurs sechees and Fleurs et plantes (dried/botanical decor, standing 'botanical decor' exclusion); Boutons et deco de porte (door hardware); Rangements decoratifs siblings Paniers et corbeilles/Paniers a linge/Rangements a bijoux/Boites (storage-primary); all Accessoires de Salle de Bains items (soap dispensers, toothbrush holders, toilet brush, etc. -- functional bathroom hardware, Rule 0.4); Couverts et menagere and Decoupe (cutlery/kitchen tools); Salieres poivrieres et moulins, Accessoires vin et cocktail, Dessous de plats, Corbeilles a pain et a fruits, Serviettes en papier, Plats aperitif et accessoires (functional/mixed tableware tools, excluded for safety since titles could not be checked live); Petit electromenager and all appliance children; Animaux de compagnie (pets); all furniture, bedding, textile/rug, and kids-furniture branches. Rule 0.6 overlap notes: a second, differently-hashed 'Miroirs' node exists as its own top-level nav department (miroirs-nd3b70ac27c5d3c19159b470e40e41c47eb024f3) alongside the one nested under Decoration murale (miroirs-484554f26aa42ef448cafd6fe7ad385e) extracted below -- almost certainly the same underlying mirror population reached via two entry points (same label, no qualifier difference), so only one Mirrors row is emitted, per the 'same listing under a second URL at the same level' drop rule, not Rule 0.6's keep-both case. A parallel kids/'enfant' branch (Decoration murale enfant, Miroirs enfant, Luminaires enfant) exists in the nav but was not separately extracted -- treated as a demographic facet of the same product types already covered by the main Wall Decor, Mirrors and Lighting rows rather than a distinct catalog branch; flagged here for the merge step to reconsider. Garden/outdoor lighting: Rule 0.1 applied -- Outdoor Floor Lamps, Garden Lamps and Outdoor String Lights (reached via the Luminaires department's own type breakdown) were extracted alongside 'Luminaire et eclairage exterieur' (the Jardin department's own outdoor-lighting rollup); these likely overlap in population since both trees cover outdoor lighting fixtures -- documented per Rule 0.6 rather than dropped.
